summary:
The Northern Cape is a province of South Africa, and the national record carries the country's constitutional discrimination guarantees, hate-crime statute, gender-recognition rules and corrections standards. What follows is specific to the province.

On the night of 14 May 2024, Jo-Ann Isaks, a 27-year-old transgender woman, was found dead in her burning room in the Paballelo location of Upington. She had multiple stab wounds to the upper body. A family member noticed the fire at about 23:00. Police in the ZF Mgcawu District confirmed a murder case had been opened, described the investigation as at a critical stage and reported no arrests; the same statement identified her publicly by a male name. Jenny Sambok, an LGBTIQ+ leader in the district, said the community in the ZF Mgcawu region had been shaken.

Karabelo Pudumo, an 18-year-old transgender Grade 10 learner at Pescodia High School in Kimberley, the provincial capital, was stabbed to death on 1 June 2024. A man she had been drinking with allegedly turned on her after realising she was transgender and stabbed her more than 20 times. A suspect was reportedly arrested, a detail the outlet reporting the case could not confirm with the authorities. More than 300 children and community members attended a memorial service at the school. Her death was the second suspected hate-crime murder of a transgender person in the province in under a month.

A third LGBTIQ+ resident, Lazarus Ikaneng Thomas, a 50-year-old gay man, was murdered in September 2024. The three deaths are raw counts for one province in one year, and the sources provide no per-capita or general homicide rate against which to measure them.

Organised community presence in the province is recent. The first Northern Cape Pride was held on 30 November 2024 at the Galeshewe Open Air Arena in Kimberley under the theme 'Pride with a Purpose', with a morning parade, speakers and community activities. Pride Committee member Tebogo Makwati called it a historic moment for the province.
tangentialFactors:
The two transgender killings occurred in different districts of the province, one around Upington in the north-west and one in the Kimberley area, so the documented lethal risk is not confined to a single town or district.

The province's first Pride event took place only in November 2024, which indicates that organised LGBTIQ+ infrastructure here is more recent than in provinces with long-established Pride events.

The September 2024 killing of a gay man shows that lethal anti-LGBTIQ+ violence in the province is not limited to transgender targets, while the two documented transgender deaths share the specific pattern of a victim attacked after her gender identity became known.
localsOnly:
More than 300 children and community members attended the memorial service at Pescodia High School in Kimberley after Karabelo Pudumo's death, and the district LGBTIQ+ leadership in the ZF Mgcawu region publicly registered the shock felt in Upington after Jo-Ann Isaks was killed.

Accountability for residents remains open. No arrests had been reported in the Isaks case at the time of reporting, and the reported arrest of a suspect in Pudumo's killing could not be confirmed with the authorities by the outlet that published it.

The inaugural Northern Cape Pride was organised by a local Pride committee as a community event at the Galeshewe Open Air Arena in Kimberley, with a parade, speakers and activities.
outOfScopeNotes:
Neither the Isaks nor the Pudumo killing has been judicially established as a hate crime. Both are described in the reporting as suspected hate crimes, and the motive in each rests on witness and community accounts rather than on a court finding.

The arrest of a suspect in the Pudumo case is unverified, and no arrest had been reported in the Isaks case at the time of publication. The current status of either investigation is not established by the sources reviewed.

The sources give no per-capita or general homicide rate for the Northern Cape, so the three 2024 LGBTIQ+ killings cannot be compared with the province's background rate of lethal violence.

Lazarus Ikaneng Thomas was a gay man, not a transgender person. His killing is recorded as part of the province's 2024 LGBTIQ+ violence pattern and not as a transgender-specific incident.
